walkthroughs.body_html: UN founded 1945 (51 founding members); now 193. Six principal organs include Security Council (5 permanent veto powers), General Assembly, ICJ. Budget 2024 around $3.6 billion regular plus $6.4 billion peacekeeping. 16 active peacekeeping missions (e.g. MINUSCA in CAR).

UDHR (1948) drafted by Eleanor Roosevelt's commission. 30 articles cover civil, political, economic, social, cultural rights. Followed by ICCPR and ICESCR (1966, binding). Universal Periodic Review covers all 193 states every 4.5 years.

Rome Statute 1998 created ICC; operational 2002. 124 state parties; USA, China, India, Russia not. Issued arrest warrant for Putin (2023) over Ukraine deportations. Convicted Lubanga (DRC) 2012 for child soldiers. Critics note overwhelming focus on Africa.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a megacity and a world city?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
Megacities and world cities are the same thing.
A megacity is defined by population (over 10 million); a world city is defined by global economic and cultural influence (e.g. New York, London) — so a city can be one without the other.
A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
Climate change only happens in summer.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
